notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in it counts as correct for this topic_id. evaluate_verdicts.py still records the exact verdict produced for the confusion matrix -- this list only controls what counts as correct.

A null acceptable_verdicts marks a topic this file does not score for verdict accuracy: sam_registration_active_at_offer, technical_medical_gas_regulatory_proof, and sdvosb_vosb_certification_status_at_submission, since all three are is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json and never get a verdict from a correctly-behaving pipeline.

The application deliberately varies its error types: compliant (11 topics), non_compliant across different failure shapes -- total omissions (cylinder replacement cost, difficult-to-fill flagging) and an explicit but mistaken self-exemption (VAAR 852.219-76 certificate declined based on a misreading of which sentence the requirement's 'when applicable' qualifier attaches to) -- insufficient_information (a tracking plan missing 2 of 7 required elements, a PMP missing 1 of 6 elements, a past performance reference missing the dollar value field, a phase-in strategy missing the Delivery Plan component, and silence on SF-1449 form completion), and two contradictory claims of different shapes: a completeness claim contradicted by a later walk-back (the Schedule of Items described as fully priced in one section but as having pending/unpriced items in another), and a factual capability conflict (an exclusive single-supplier sourcing claim in one section versus a two-independent-supplier backup claim in another).
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone; true_requirements.json is the source of truth if the two diverge.

Three acceptable_verdicts lists were broadened after a first real pipeline run: cylinder_replacement_cost_in_proposal now also accepts contradictory, and price_schedule_attachment_c_completed now also accepts non_compliant -- both topics sit next to the deliberately engineered pending-four-items pricing inconsistency, and the model consistently connected that same fact pattern to these neighboring topics in a defensible way. quote_identification_and_solicitation_number now also accepts insufficient_information -- the source text bundles offeror/solicitation-number identification together with a requirement that the quote be 'complete, self-sufficient', and the model reasonably read the admitted four-pending-item gap as violating that completeness clause, even though the offeror-identification part itself is satisfied.

primary_verdict / primary_verdict_source (added by SFT data-prep pass): a single training-target label per topic, additive -- acceptable_verdicts is unchanged and remains the source of truth for verdict-accuracy scoring. primary_verdict is the pipeline's own correct prediction where one exists (source: pipeline_prediction), else acceptable_verdicts[0] (source: acceptable_verdicts_first). null for topics with acceptable_verdicts: null (excluded from SFT training, same as they're excluded from verdict scoring).

verdicts.description: Offerors must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of offer.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- actual SAM registration/active status cannot be confirmed by reading the application text, only by checking SAM.gov directly.

verdicts.description: The contractor must comply with the delivery frequencies specified per delivery location as outlined in Attachment A.
verdicts.rationale: Application explicitly commits to complying with the delivery frequency specified per location in Attachment A.

evidence.quote:
We commit to complying with the delivery frequency
specified per location in Attachment A for all seven facility groups.

verdicts.description: The contractor must have a facility and/or resources physically located in the geographic areas in which they will provide supplies.
verdicts.rationale: Application states staffed depots in Fargo, ND and Sioux Falls, SD plus a satellite dispatch point in Minneapolis, MN, placing resources within the geographic areas served.

evidence.quote:
Northern Plains Medical Gases operates staffed depots in Fargo, ND and
Sioux Falls, SD, with a satellite dispatch point in Minneapolis, MN,
placing resources within each of the geographic areas served under this
solicitation.

verdicts.description: The contractor's proposal must include the cylinder replacement cost for each item listed on Attachment C.
verdicts.rationale: Application never mentions a cylinder replacement cost for lost or damaged contractor-owned cylinders; the price schedule section addresses only per-item pricing and the 90-day firm-price term.

verdicts.description: The contractor must submit a cylinder tracking plan with their proposal for cylinders being delivered to and from the ordering activity, covering data-entry method and mechanism, when and how the Government can extract data, what data is stored, access limits, and any Government-network connection requirements. If the contractor's tracking system is impending/not yet fully operational, the proposal must include an implementation timeline coinciding with the phase-in timeline.
verdicts.rationale: Application describes a barcode-based delivery-side tracking plan covering the data-entry method/mechanism and on-demand data access, but never addresses two of the plan's required elements -- access limits for Government employees and any technology requiring connection to the Government network -- so the plan as described is incomplete.

evidence.quote:
For cylinders in transit to and from ordering activities, we will use a
barcode-based tracking system (method: handheld barcode scanners at
pickup and delivery, data stored in a cloud portal) that allows ordering
activity POCs on-demand access to view and extract delivery and location
data for all cylinders moving in and out of their facility.

verdicts.description: Although not required, if the contractor has a system for tracking medical gas cylinders within an ordering activity's facility after delivery, the contractor must submit a tracking plan with their proposal covering the same items as the delivery-side tracking plan.
verdicts.rationale: This sub-requirement is conditional on the contractor having a facility-side tracking system after delivery. The application affirmatively states it does not operate such a system, so the condition never applies and the plan is correctly not submitted.

evidence.quote:
We do not currently operate a system for tracking medical gas cylinders
within an ordering activity's facility after delivery, and are therefore
not submitting a facility-side tracking plan with this proposal.

verdicts.description: The contractor must submit in their proposal their available on-demand reporting capabilities (usage, cost, and cylinder tracking reports), including how the data is collected, distributed, and viewed.
verdicts.rationale: Application describes on-demand usage, cost, and cylinder-tracking reporting through a cloud portal, and states how the data is collected/viewed (web portal or Excel export), covering the required content.

evidence.quote:
Northern Plains Medical Gases will provide on-demand usage, cost, and
cylinder-tracking reports through the same cloud portal referenced above,
covering actual and average deliveries by week, month, and year and by
gas type; actual and average billing data by week, month, and year per
medical gas; and perpetual delivery, pick-up, and location data per
cylinder. Reports will be viewable through the web portal or exported to

verdicts.description: The contractor must identify in their proposal any medical gases that can be classified as difficult to fill or likely to be placed on backorder, by highlighting the item in Attachment C and providing a statement justifying the classification.
verdicts.rationale: Application never identifies or flags any medical gases as difficult to fill or likely to be placed on backorder, and never references highlighting any item in Attachment C for this purpose.

verdicts.description: The contractor must submit a Project Management Plan (PMP) with their proposal demonstrating understanding of the scope, schedule, and service level requirements, including at minimum a communications and task matrix, an identified individual responsible for deliverables, a preliminary delivery/install/user acceptance schedule, a time estimate per critical task, an outline of progress-tracking processes, and an approach to identifying and resolving potential project problems.
verdicts.rationale: Application's Project Management Plan section addresses the communications/task matrix, the responsible individual, and a preliminary schedule with time estimates, but never describes an approach to identifying warning signs of potential project problems and their resolution process, so the PMP as described is missing one required element.

evidence.quote:
Our Project Management Plan assigns a single point of contact, Dana
Whitfield, who will coordinate onboarding, task order communications, and
identify and delineate the roles and responsibilities of our dispatch and
billing staff. Dana Whitfield is also responsible for ensuring contract
deliverables are provided on time. A preliminary delivery, install, and

dependencies and an estimate of how much time each critical task is
expected to take through the first 60 days of performance.

verdicts.rationale: Application explicitly agrees to hold prices firm for 90 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers, matching the requirement.

verdicts.description: The SF-1449 must be submitted fully completed, with the offeror completing page 1 sections 30a, 30b, and 30c.
verdicts.rationale: Application never mentions the SF-1449 form or confirms that page 1 sections 30a-30c were completed; a cover-letter-style quote of this kind is silent on the administrative form itself, which may be completed as a separate attachment not reproduced in this text.

verdicts.description: If solicitation amendments are issued, the contractor must acknowledge all amendments to the solicitation.
verdicts.rationale: Application states no amendments to the solicitation had been issued as of the date of the quote, so there is nothing to acknowledge; the conditional requirement is not triggered.

verdicts.description: Offeror must provide narrative in as much detail as possible to fully explain the existing operational capability to meet the requirements contained in the Statement of Work.
verdicts.rationale: Application provides a narrative on operational capability, citing eleven years of medical-gas cylinder delivery and rental experience across the relevant states and asserting capability to meet the SOW.

verdicts.description: Offeror must provide procedures or documentation demonstrating the ability to navigate through emergency situations, shortages, and any other form of supply chain interruptions.
verdicts.rationale: The Depots and Delivery section states that all specialty and bulk gases are sourced through an exclusive agreement with a single filler, while the Continuity of Operations section states the opposite -- that backup supply agreements exist with two independent fillers. An exclusive single-supplier arrangement and a two-supplier backup arrangement cannot both be true.

evidence.quote:
All specialty and bulk medical gases offered under this contract are

Continuity of Operations: In the event of a supply-chain interruption, we

verdicts.description: Offeror must demonstrate the innovative use of a cylinder tracking and management system, as part of the Technical Capability narrative.
verdicts.rationale: Application demonstrates the innovative use of a cylinder tracking and management system by cross-referencing the barcode-based system described under Cylinder Tracking.

evidence.quote:
Cylinder Management: As described above under Cylinder Tracking, our

verdicts.description: Offeror must provide proof that all medical gases conform to USP and National Formulary specifications and that the contractor and its medical gas manufacturers/fillers are registered with the FDA.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- whether the gases genuinely conform to USP/National Formulary specifications and whether the manufacturers/fillers are genuinely FDA-registered cannot be confirmed by reading the application's own representation of those facts.

verdicts.rationale: Application's phase-in strategy addresses a Project Communications Plan and an Implementation Plan, but never mentions a Delivery Plan or any milestone dates/timelines demonstrating the ability to meet the effective date or the 60-calendar-day requirement, so one of the three required components is missing.

verdicts.description: To receive Veterans Involvement evaluation credit, an offeror must be listed at the time of submission of offers and at time of award as a certified SDVOSB/VOSB in the SBA certification database.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- whether the offeror is genuinely listed in the SBA certification database cannot be confirmed by reading the application's own certification statement, only by checking the SBA database directly.

verdicts.description: If the offeror is a large business proposing to use certified SDVOSBs or VOSBs as subcontractors and elects to receive evaluation consideration under this factor, the proposal must state the names of the certified SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractors, a description of their services/supplies, and approximate dollar values.
verdicts.rationale: This sub-requirement only applies to a large business electing SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractor credit. The application states all work will be performed with the offeror's own personnel and equipment and that no subcontractors are proposed, so the triggering condition (proposing SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractors) does not apply.

evidence.quote:
Northern Plains Medical Gases will perform 100% of the work identified in
the Statement of Work and Contract Administration with its own personnel
and equipment; no subcontractors, similarly situated entities, or other
performing parties are proposed.

verdicts.description: In response to the Limitations on Subcontracting factor (when applicable), offerors must submit a breakdown of the work identified in the Statement of Work and Contract Administration tasks, identifying which work will be performed by the prime contractor, any similarly situated entity, and any other subcontractors.
verdicts.rationale: Application states 100% of the work will be performed by the prime contractor with no subcontractors or similarly situated entities, which is itself the required breakdown of who performs the work.

evidence.quote:
Northern Plains Medical Gases will perform 100% of the work identified in
the Statement of Work and Contract Administration with its own personnel
and equipment; no subcontractors, similarly situated entities, or other
performing parties are proposed.

verdicts.description: Offerors must submit a completed copy of VAAR 852.219-76 -- VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting -- Certificate of Compliance for Supplies and Products with the submission package.
verdicts.rationale: Application explicitly declines to include the VAAR 852.219-76 certificate, reasoning that it does not apply because the offeror proposes no subcontractors and is not a large business electing SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractor credit. The requirement's own text ties that 'when applicable' qualifier only to the preceding subcontracting-breakdown sentence, not to the certificate sentence, which is unconditional -- so the certificate is still required and its absence is non-compliant, not a correctly-recognized exemption.

evidence.quote:
As we are not proposing to use any
subcontractors and are not a large business electing SDVOSB/VOSB
subcontractor credit, we have not included a VAAR 852.219-76 Certificate
of Compliance with this submission.
